audit.automatic_entry: RECOVERY_ENTRY is recorded from HP3 no-viable evidence without inventing a session identity
audit.identity_binding: accepted-command audit records carry authorization epoch, session nonce, command sequence, request ID, and principal SHA-256 but never authorization proof bytes
audit.slot_transitions: each durable staging, verification, rejection, or TRIAL metadata commit emits SLOT_TRANSITION with the bounded slot and artifact SHA-256
audit.terminal_rule: every accepted HP4.3 command produces exactly one retained terminal through the HP4.1 first-terminal-wins core

candidate_staging.activation: a completely verified candidate becomes durable TRIAL before REBOOT_HANDOFF; the next boot remains owned by HP3
candidate_staging.deterministic_empty_selection: when active and last-good are NONE, the existing HP3 inactive-slot selector chooses A
candidate_staging.failure_mode: RECOVERY for every recovery-origin abort, timeout, resource denial, stream failure, verifier denial, or journal failure before handoff
candidate_staging.resource_admission: the unchanged HP1 exclusive gate requires 98,304 fixed bytes plus 65,536 update bytes and a 98,304-byte largest block
verification: inner bundle hash and bundle policy
HP2 running-host compatibility and resource placement

command_authority.host_source_rule: RECOVERY and UPDATE sources and their HP1 priorities are derived inside wdc_admin; application, event, capability, and native-refinement callers cannot select or reserve them
command_authority.replay_rule: unauthorized, stale, replayed, out-of-order, expired, malformed, busy, or wrong-state requests are rejected before a ticket, replay advance, mode change, or slot mutation

component.firmware_link: firmware/main/app_main.c calls wdc_admin_recovery_link_anchor before the application pthread is created
component.update_extension: firmware/components/wdc_admin/wdc_admin_update.c returns recovery-origin failures and aborts to RECOVERY

deferred: HP4.4 adversarial administration and recovery seal
UART or USB serial driver and physical-board execution
Wi-Fi, TLS, HTTP, MQTT, or another network transport
external ESP32 provider or Pulse-core change
host-firmware, bootloader, factory-host, or partition-table OTA
production signing, authentication, provisioning, or key lifecycle

entry.administrative: an accepted ENTER_RECOVERY transitions NORMAL to QUIESCE and requires positive guest and native-refinement quiesce/unload evidence before RECOVERY
entry.automatic: an HP3 BOOT_RECOVERY result with selected and fallback slots NONE, no reboot request, no application launch, and metadata active/last-good NONE initializes RECOVERY directly
entry.automatic_failure_rule: malformed or metadata-inconsistent boot evidence fails initialization without manufacturing recovery authority

reboot.no_viable_candidate: FAILED terminal, RECOVERY retained, and no reboot loop
reboot.safe_guard: REBOOT requires recovery idle state, no loaded application/refinements, an active CONFIRMED or TRIAL record, complete read-only artifact verification, HP2 prelaunch admission, and unchanged metadata

legal_transitions: QUIESCE -> RECOVERY after positive host-owned unload evidence
QUIESCE -> NORMAL on entry failure or timeout
RECOVERY -> UPDATE after HP1 admission and inactive-slot stage begin
UPDATE -> RECOVERY on recovery-origin abort, failure, or timeout
RECOVERY -> RECOVERY on STATUS or idle ABORT
RECOVERY -> REBOOT_HANDOFF only after read-only HP3 viability proof
UPDATE -> REBOOT_HANDOFF only after durable TRIAL read-back
state_machine.prohibited: RECOVERY never transitions directly to NORMAL; application execution resumes only after reboot through HP3
